name: copy
note: review: Mirror: copyShallow writes the bound-method branch as a new MethodType(f, s), but CPython reaches it through method.__reduce__ (Objects/classobject.c:91-116), which returns getattr(__self__, __func__.__name__), so copy(m) can be a different object or AttributeError, and it has no copyreg.dispatch_table step (:84-86) and no __reduce__ fallback (:92-94); property: CopyShallow pins only the list, tuple and hooked-error/str/Error branches, so a copy that fails on dicts, instances, frozendicts, a succeeding __copy__ or a reduce tuple (never linked to reconShallow) still satisfies it, and the pickle-reduce refutation runs only reconShallow, not copyShallow.

name: deepcopy
note: review: Mirror: the model has no copyreg.dispatch_table step (:139-141), cannot express __reduce_ex__ = None falling back to __reduce__ (:143-149), and drops _keep_alive (:161), whose memo[id(memo)] entry a caller-supplied memo and every __deepcopy__(memo) can see; property: no theorem pins the issubclass(cls, type) branch (:132-133), a succeeding __deepcopy__ and its memo entry (:137, :159-160), a reduce string (:153-154) or a raising reductor, so a deepcopy that errors or memoizes wrongly on those paths passes every listed entry.

name: _keep_alive
note: review: The no-behaviour reason does not apply: the body writes memo[id(memo)] = [..., x] into the memo, which the caller of deepcopy(x, memo) and every __deepcopy__(memo) can see, and which deepcopy(memo, memo) returns at :125-126; it also keeps temporary objects alive so their ids are not reused within one pass, which the model avoids only because its cells are never freed.

name: _reconstruct
signature: _reconstruct(x, memo, func, args, state=None, listiter=None, dictiter=None, *, deepcopy=deepcopy)
note: review: Mirror: reconRest calls __setstate__ for a state cell that is None (atom 0, the model's own None per stateStep), skipping the `if state is not None` of :252 (it is checked only inside stateStep), y.__dict__.update(state) accepts only a dict cell where CPython takes any mapping or iterable of pairs, and is evaluated after the state rather than before (an empty state on a y without __dict__ is AttributeError in CPython and ok in the model), and listiter/dictiter are plain lists that cannot raise; property: ReconstructSteps' third conjunct and ReconRestItems' fifth and sixth claim __setstate__ runs (or its error propagates) for every st, including None, which is false for CPython when the reduce state is None.

name: replace
note: review: replaceOp takes the already-computed result of func(obj, **changes) as an Option (Py β), so it does not mirror the obj.__class__ lookup, getattr(cls, '__replace__', None) (including an explicit None), or the call with changes (:296-300); the two conjuncts are rfl on that one-line match, which any function returning its argument or a TypeError also satisfies.
